content: The bass DI is re-amped through an Ampeg B-15. Mix bus: a BAX EQ, an SSL bus compressor, a tape machine emulation, a Gullfoss EQ, and a FabFilter Pro-L2 limiter. Automation makes special moments and separates the sections of a song.

content: The band records live with real instruments and seldom cuts takes together. The aim is a simple, minimal sound: each instrument contributes and no instrument dominates. Grooves have priority over melody.
parameters: A compressor plug-in with the name of the band (Vulf Compressor). Early sessions on 2-inch tape

content: Older Knower drum tracks used one cheap microphone.
parameters: A conference microphone of less than 20 dollars, between snare and bass drum near the floor-tom edge. Result: quiet cymbals; kick and snare with the same punch. Later he added microphones but kept this one

content: A small, half-open bass drum that is easy to mix.

content: He keeps mixes gritty on purpose. He records, mixes and masters at home.
parameters: "I wanted it crusty on purpose because it grooves way harder." Garage, living room, bedroom; no studios. One song was mixed about 70 times

content: Big groups are recorded and filmed in his house.
parameters: Drum kit on the stairs; winds downstairs; singers on the balcony; 4 to 6 takes for each video. Strings: 23 players, or a trio with a click track; the players did not hear the song

content: A garage with no windows and a few microphones.
parameters: About 1.5 years of work. Drum tracks of at least 3 songs were recorded on a phone. Final studio work at Larrabee, North Hollywood

content: Objects lie on the drums and cymbals to shorten the sound.
parameters: Pretzels on the hi-hat; toilet paper or a towel on the snare; splash cymbals on the snare heads. Bass drum and floor tom heavily damped; hi-hat taped. Long sounds would blur the fast notes

content: He tries to make live drums sound "as electronic as possible".
parameters: Snare tuned and played to sound electronic. An electronic sound on the backbeats; a very dry sound on the notes between. Plug-ins on the drums in Ableton

content: Muffling sheets lie on all snares.

content: Toms are special sounds. Hi-hats are dry like a drum machine.
parameters: Floor tom with a sheet: short, like cardboard. Rack tom 10 x 8 tuned very high: "as alien as possible". 14-inch hi-hat: very dry, in control when open; tip and butt of the stick give two sounds

content: Three members are recording engineers with their own studio.

content: "If the sound can be right, then you can really play anything."
parameters: He treats the kit like a DJ or a programmer. Short stacks; dark cymbals; drum sound changed by heads and muffling

content: He made detailed home demos and charts. The band replaced each demo part.

item: Recipe for the tight rhythm tone
content: The 'djent' tone is a boost pedal in front of a high-gain amp with less gain than a player expects, and noise gates that make the rig silent between the notes.
parameters: (1) As little amp gain as possible: stop when palm mutes start to sustain. (2) Amp EQ at 12 o'clock, then mids a little down and highs up. (3) Overdrive pedal before the amp: drive at or near zero, level high; it tightens the low end. (4) Noise gates on the pedal and on the amp. (5) Tape or a damper over the strings at the nut

content: The rhythm guitars give up the low end to kick and bass. Their character sits in the upper mids.
parameters: High-pass at about 100 Hz, up to 120 or 140 Hz for low tunings. 150 to 250 Hz: the palm-mute 'chug' zone; cut a little if muddy. Cut near 400 Hz against a boxy sound. 800 Hz to 1.5 kHz: the 'grind' of Meshuggah and Periphery tones. 2 to 4 kHz: pick attack. 5 to 9 kHz: fizz; remove with a narrow notch

content: The kick is reinforced or replaced by samples for a machine-like, even attack, and it is built from layers. The records use drum samples, but the cymbals stay real.
parameters: Kick layers: click (high-pass at 100 to 300 Hz, boost at 2 to 8 kHz), body (boost at 60 to 100 Hz by 2 to 4 dB), sub (sine at 40 to 60 Hz or tuned to the key, low-pass at 80 to 100 Hz). High-pass the kick at 30 to 40 Hz with 18 to 24 dB an octave; cut 200 to 500 Hz. Beater click in a dense mix: 3 to 5 kHz. Snare: body 200 to 250 Hz, crack 900 Hz to 1 kHz, wires 5 kHz. Cymbals: 6 to 10 kHz

item: Bass guitar: role and two-band chain
content: The bass doubles the guitar riff one octave lower and adds its own grit. The mix splits it in two tracks: a clean, firm low track and a distorted high track.
parameters: Low track: low-pass at 200 Hz, high-pass at 30 to 40 Hz, strong compression below 150 Hz, about 4 dB of ducking from the kick. Grit track: high-pass at 200 to 300 Hz before the distortion, boost at 1.5 to 4 kHz for the pick 'clank', level 6 to 10 dB below the low track. Bass weight at 80 to 120 Hz with the kick at 60 Hz; growl at 400 to 800 Hz. Meshuggah: pick and overdrive pedals. Reference bass of the style: a fanned-fret bass with a low B string

content: The rhythm part is recorded twice with the same tone, one take on each side. Parts are recorded one after the other in short takes and edited hard. Some bands react against this and record live.
parameters: Thall: two takes 'so tight it sounds like mono'; takes of two or three bars. Animals as Leaders: no recording together in one room; the drummer plays to the finished guitars. Meshuggah 2016: guitar, bass, drums and voice recorded together, no edits. Parrhesia: tracked with plugins, then recorded again with real amps. A plugin 'doubler' can imitate the second take

item: Standard mix values not found in a source (estimate)
content: Standard practice, not confirmed in a source read here. No source gave a loudness value.
parameters: Estimate: rhythm guitars 100% left and right; four takes (two on each side) for the heaviest sections; guitar low-pass at 8 to 12 kHz; bass, kick, snare and lead in the centre; lead delay of a quarter or dotted eighth note (300 to 450 ms) at a low level; lead reverb of 1.5 to 2.5 s; master loudness about -9 to -6 LUFS integrated

content: A dark, clicking tone from an old amp model, a mid boost and heavy EQ after a dark cabinet response.
parameters: Amp model 'Big Bottom' of a Line 6 Pod, named as the guitar sound of Meshuggah's Catch Thirtythree: gain 50%, bass 15%, mids 85%, treble 60%, presence 70% (a second source says: gain just past the halfway point, bass rolled off, mids and treble high). Boost before the amp: mid frequency 51%, treble 60%, bass 60%; it adds bass and upper mids and does not cut lows as a Tube Screamer does. Compressor: slow attack, fast release. Very dark cabinet impulse response, then a large EQ; mid boost on the mid channel only

content: Abasi blends two amp models: one modern and tight in the low end, one vintage with less gain and more mids. The thump tone is cleaner and needs a fast gate and a compressor.
parameters: 2013 amp models: rhythm Friedman BE + 'Dizzy VH4'; lead Friedman BE + Plexi; slap Cameron + Friedman BE; clean with some compression; effects: a small multi-tap delay, sometimes reverb. Thump tone: gate with the shortest attack; compressor; soft-crunch Marshall type + Fender Bassman type; controls at 12 o'clock, treble a little higher; cut near 500 Hz; single-coil or coil-split pickup. Later: real EL34 high-gain head with a noise gate, in stereo

content: The guitar goes direct through his signature plugin. Clean and lead tones stay as he recorded them; the heavy rhythm guitars are sent again through real amps.
parameters: Cleans and leads: plugin compressor, drive and amp as recorded; the mixer changes only EQ, delay and reverb. Rhythm guitars: re-amped through a 5150 and a Marshall JCM 800 or 900. Lesson tone: gain 3, bass 7, middle 6, treble 7, reverb 2; clean neck pickup, then bridge humbucker; long delay and much reverb on leads

item: Amps and clarity of the low string
content: Very high gain, with the whole chain built to control it. The clarity of the lowest string comes from the pick attack, the long scale and a pickup that adds no power.
parameters: About 1999: Mesa/Boogie Dual Rectifier in the studio, wax-potted pickups, a noise gate in the effects loop. 2016: a modified Marshall, a 120 W head and a 50 W signature head for rhythm; Axe-Fx only for solos and cleans; a boost pedal with a sweepable bass filter. Scale 27 to 29.4 inches. For very low tunings also: high string action. The eighth string needs its own pick attack; the pick angle changes the tone. Down strokes alone give the hardest attack (Abasi rarely uses them)

content: Clean parts use compression and time effects. They are the contrast to the dry, gated riff tone.
parameters: Meshuggah (about 1999): compressor, stereo chorus and a multi-effect. Thall: clean signal with a little reverb and delay; with plugins, sometimes no cabinet simulation. Abasi: clean amp blended with a piezo-like voice, with compression. Plini: warm neck-pickup tone; chorus with a 1980s option in his plugin
source: gw-meshuggah-sound; gw-thall; ndsp-abasi; pg-aal-2013; gw-plini-lesson; ndsp-plini

item: Studio method of the Mwandishi band
content: The band plays live in the studio at night. Effects are added after. Tape edits are rare. Synthesizers are overdubbed later (1972) or patched before a live take (1973).
parameters: 1971: small room with an 8-track machine set up for 16 tracks; one take; flanging added to one of the two drummers; the producer works the wah pedal of the guitar by hand. 1973: live with few overdubs; about one week in the studio; edits bring in soloists; reverb on trumpet; echo and reverb on trombone

content: Layered synthesizer bass to a click. Band takes in one pass.
parameters: September 1973, evening sessions, two studios in San Francisco. Synthesizer bass recorded alone to a click. 1974: Actual Proof in one take; the bass of Palm Grease in one take. Quadraphonic mix in 1974 with one more keyboard line

content: Room sound, few takes, and a bass player who mixes.
parameters: Tiled echo room for ambience; microphones not close. Birdland: one take. A Remark You Made: 1 or 2 takes and one overdub. Havona: almost no overdubs. The bass player did much of the mix (reverb, drum sound)

content: Layer one or more snares with a clap. Add reverb for space and width.

content: The kick must hit higher in the spectrum than the sub. A very deep 808 kick does not work over a sine sub. The tail of the kick is short.
parameters: Kick above the sub band of 30 to 60 Hz

content: Usual values.
parameters: Kick fundamental 50 to 70 Hz with a click at 2 to 5 kHz; snare body 180 to 250 Hz with noise above 5 kHz. Estimate

content: A compressor on the sub or on the full bass has the kick as its key input. A muted closed hi-hat on the kick pattern gives a shorter duck.
parameters: The bass ducks on each kick

content: Usual values.
parameters: Gain reduction 3 to 6 dB for a clean mix and 8 to 12 dB for pumping that you can hear; release 80 to 150 ms. Estimate

content: Each part has its own band.
parameters: Sub 30 to 60 Hz; narrow cuts in the bass at 100 to 300 Hz; bass presence at 1 to 3 kHz; leads at 200 to 800 Hz; the energy below 100 Hz is kept for the drop

content: Upward and downward compression in three bands at the same time.
parameters: Ableton Multiband Dynamics preset OTT: crossovers 88.3 Hz and 2.5 kHz; input +5.2 dB on each band; downward ratio: high band infinity to 1, mid and low 66.7 to 1; upward ratio 4 to 1 on each band; output +10.3 dB low and high, +5.7 dB mid.
